text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.88% today as oil prices firmed slightly—U.S. crude holding at $89.53 per barrel and global Brent at $92.94—after geopolitical tensions in the Middle East intensified. Reports of Iranian tankers hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries reminded markets that supply disruptions remain a real risk, supporting crude prices and the earnings of oil producers like COP.

The move also comes as refinery-related trades have been cooling (the "epic boom" in that sector is unwinding), which could be redirecting some investor focus back toward pure-play oil producers rather than refiners. That said, the stock remains down 0.66% over two weeks, suggesting today's bounce is modest relief within a broader period of weakness.
